questions.solution:
( m1d1 × h1  ) / ( w1 ) = ( m2d2 × h2 ) / ( w2 )                              

( P × 18 / w ) = ( p × 5 + ( P+Q ) ×  13/5 )

= 65P = 13P + 13Q = 52P = 13Q = 4P = Q

= ( P × 18 / work ) = ( Q × D2  ) / ( 66 × 2/3 % ) work

= ( P × 18 ) = ( 4P × D2 ) / (2/3) = D2 = 18 / (2/3) = 3 days.

questions.question: The areas of three adjacent faces of a cuboidal solid block of wax are 216 cm 2 , 96 cm 2 and 144 cm 2 . It is melted and 8 cubes of the same size are formed from it. What is the lateral surface area (in cm 2 ) of 3 such cubes?
questions.questionHtml: The areas of three adjacent faces of a cuboidal solid block of wax are 216 cm<sup>2</sup>, 96 cm<sup>2</sup> and 144 cm<sup>2</sup>. It is melted and 8 cubes of the same size are formed from it. What is the lateral surface area (in cm<sup>2</sup>) of 3 such cubes?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Volume of cuboid = √(216 × 96 × 144) = 1728 cm3

Volume of 1 small cube = 1728 ÷ 8 = 216 cm3

Side of small cube (a) = (216)1/3 = 6 cm

Lateral Surface Area (LSA) of 3 cubes = 3 × 4a2 = 12 × 36 = 432 cm2

∴ The correct answer is 432 cm2.

Alternate Method

Given:

Area of face 1 (lb) = 216 cm2

Area of face 2 (bh) = 96 cm2

Area of face 3 (lh) = 144 cm2

Formula Used:

Volume of cuboid (V) = √(Area1 × Area2 × Area3)

Lateral Surface Area of cube = 4 × side2

Calculations:

⇒ Volume of cuboid = √(216 × 96 × 144)

⇒ Volume = √(2,985,984) = 1728 cm3

⇒ Volume of one small cube = 1728 ÷ 8 = 216 cm3

⇒ Side3 = 216

⇒ Side (a) = 6 cm

⇒ Lateral Surface Area of 1 cube = 4 × 62 = 4 × 36 = 144 cm2

⇒ Lateral Surface Area of 3 cubes = 3 × 144 = 432 cm2

∴ The correct answer is 432 cm2.

Additional Information

Volume and Face Areas of a Cuboid

If A1, A2, and A3 are the areas of three adjacent faces of a cuboid, then its Volume V = √(A1 × A2 × A3).

Surface Areas of a Cube

For a cube with side 'a', the Lateral Surface Area (area of 4 vertical walls) is 4a2 and the Total Surface Area is 6a2.

Volume Conservation

When a solid object is melted and recast into several smaller objects, the total volume of all smaller objects equals the volume of the original solid.

questions.question: The ratio of the incomes of A and B in 2020 was 5 ∶ 4. The ratios of their individual incomes in 2020 and 2021 were 4 ∶ 5 and 2 ∶ 3, respectively. If the total income A and B in 2021 was Rs.7,05,600, then what was the income (in Rs.) of B in 2021?
questions.questionHtml: The ratio of the incomes of A and B in 2020 was 5 ∶ 4. The ratios of their individual incomes in 2020 and 2021 were 4 ∶ 5 and 2 ∶ 3, respectively. If the total income A and B in 2021 was Rs.7,05,600, then what was the income (in Rs.) of B in 2021?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Income A : B (2020) = 5 : 4

Change ratios: A (4 : 5) → A (2021) = 5 × (5 ÷ 4) = 6.25 units

Change ratios: B (2 : 3) → B (2021) = 4 × (3 ÷ 2) = 6 units

Income A : B (2021) = 6.25 : 6 = 25 : 24 (Total = 49 units)

B's 2021 income = (24 ÷ 49) × 7,05,600 = 24 × 14,400 = Rs. 3,45,600

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 3,45,600.

Alternate Method

Given:

Income ratio A : B (2020) = 5 : 4

Individual income ratio A (2020 : 2021) = 4 : 5

Individual income ratio B (2020 : 2021) = 2 : 3

Total income of A and B in 2021 = Rs. 7,05,600

Formula Used:

New Income = Old Income × (New Ratio Part ÷ Old Ratio Part)

Calculations:

⇒ To make the 2020 income of A (5) divisible by 4 and B (4) divisible by 2, multiply the A:B (2020) ratio by 4.

⇒ New A:B (2020) = (5 × 4) : (4 × 4) = 20 : 16

⇒ A's income in 2021 = (20 ÷ 4) × 5 = 25 units

⇒ B's income in 2021 = (16 ÷ 2) × 3 = 24 units

⇒ Total income in 2021 = 25 + 24 = 49 units

⇒ Given 49 units = 7,05,600

⇒ 1 unit = 7,05,600 ÷ 49 = 14,400

⇒ Income of B in 2021 = 24 × 14,400 = 3,45,600

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 3,45,600.

Additional Information

Ratio Normalization

When connecting ratios across different time frames, find a common multiple for the shared term (usually the base year value) to simplify calculations.

Compound Ratios

The final ratio of two variables after changes can be found by multiplying the initial ratio parts by their respective fractional change factors.

Division by Ratio

To find an individual part, use the formula: Share = (Individual Ratio ÷ Sum of Ratio Parts) × Total Value.

questions.question: In a medical transaction, 17 times the cost price is equal to 8 times the sum of the cost price and the selling price. What is the gain or loss percentage?
questions.questionHtml: In a medical transaction, 17 times the cost price is equal to 8 times the sum of the cost price and the selling price. What is the gain or loss percentage?
questions.solution:
17 C.P = 8 [C.P + S.P] ⇒ 9 C.P = 8 S.P ⇒ C.P : S.P = 8 : 9 

Profit% = [(9 - 8)/8] × 100% = 12.5%

questions.question: In an examination, B obtained 20% more marks than those obtained by A, and A obtained 10% less marks than those obtained by C. D obtained 20% more marks than those obtained by C. By what percentage are the marks obtained by D more than those obtained by A?
questions.questionHtml: In an examination, B obtained 20% more marks than those obtained by A, and A obtained 10% less marks than those obtained by C. D obtained 20% more marks than those obtained by C. By what percentage are the marks obtained by D more than those obtained by A?
questions.solution:
D obtained 20% more marks than those obtained by C ⇒ (120/100) × 100 ⇒ 120

A obtained 10% less marks than those obtained by C ⇒ (90/100) × 100 ⇒ 90

B obtained 20% more marks than those obtained by A ⇒ (120/100) × 90 ⇒ 108

The percentage of marks obtained by D more than those obtained by A = [(120 – 90)/90 × 100] ⇒ (30/90) × 100

⇒ 100/3 % ⇒  \(33\frac{1}{3} \)%

questions.question: The value of \(\frac{(2.53)^3+(2.47)^3}{25.3×25.3-624.91+24.7×24.7} \) is 5 × 10 k where the value of k is:
questions.questionHtml: The value of \(\frac{(2.53)^3+(2.47)^3}{25.3×25.3-624.91+24.7×24.7} \) is 5 × 10k where the value of k is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Identify algebraic identity: a3 + b3 = (a + b)(a2 − ab + b2).

Let a = 2.53 and b = 2.47. Then a + b = 5.

Denominator = (10a)2 − (10a × 10b) + (10b)2 = 100(a2 − ab + b2).

Expression = [(a + b)(a2 − ab + b2)] ÷ [100(a2 − ab + b2)] = (a + b) ÷ 100.

Expression = 5 ÷ 100 = 0.05 = 5 × 10−2.

∴ The correct answer is −2.

Alternate Method

Given Expression: [(2.53)3 + (2.47)3] ÷ [25.3 × 25.3 − 624.91 + 24.7 × 24.7]

Let a = 2.53 and b = 2.47

⇒ Numerator = a3 + b3

⇒ Numerator = (a + b)(a2 − ab + b2)

⇒ Numerator = (2.53 + 2.47)(2.532 − 2.53 × 2.47 + 2.472) = 5 × (2.532 − 2.53 × 2.47 + 2.472)

Now, analyze the Denominator:

⇒ 25.3 = 10 × 2.53 and 24.7 = 10 × 2.47

⇒ Denominator = (10 × 2.53)2 − 624.91 + (10 × 2.47)2

⇒ Denominator = 100 × (2.532) − 100 × (2.53 × 2.47) + 100 × (2.472) [Since 100 × 2.53 × 2.47 = 100 × 6.2491 = 624.91]

⇒ Denominator = 100 × (2.532 − 2.53 × 2.47 + 2.472)

Combining Numerator and Denominator:

⇒ Value = [5 × (2.532 − 2.53 × 2.47 + 2.472)] ÷ [100 × (2.532 − 2.53 × 2.47 + 2.472)]

⇒ Value = 5 ÷ 100 = 0.05

⇒ 5 × 10k = 0.05

⇒ 5 × 10k = 5 × 10−2

⇒ k = −2

∴ The correct answer is −2.

Additional Information

Algebraic Cube Identities

The sum of cubes is a3 + b3 = (a + b)(a2 − ab + b2) and the difference of cubes is a3 − b3 = (a − b)(a2 + ab + b2).

Decimal Scaling in Expressions

When terms are scaled by 10, the squared terms are scaled by 102 = 100 and cubed terms are scaled by 103 = 1000.

Laws of Indices

For any non-zero number a, 1/an = a−n. In this case, 1/100 = 1/102 = 10−2.

questions.question: The driver of a car, which is travelling at a speed of 75 km/h, locates a bus 80 m ahead of him, travelling in the same direction. After 15 seconds, he finds that the bus is 40 m behind the car. What is the speed of the bus (in km/h)?
questions.questionHtml: The driver of a car, which is travelling at a speed of 75 km/h, locates a bus 80 m ahead of him, travelling in the same direction. After 15 seconds, he finds that the bus is 40 m behind the car. What is the speed of the bus (in km/h)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total relative distance covered by car = Initial distance ahead + Final distance behind = 80 + 40 = 120 m.

Relative speed in m/s = Distance ÷ Time = 120 ÷ 15 = 8 m/s.

Convert relative speed to km/h = 8 × (18/5) = 28.8 km/h.

Speed of the bus = Car speed − Relative speed = 75 − 28.8 = 46.2 km/h.

∴ The correct answer is 46.2 km/h.

Alternate Method

Given:

Speed of car (Vc) = 75 km/h

Initial distance of bus ahead = 80 m

Final distance of bus behind = 40 m

Time taken (t) = 15 seconds

Formula Used:

Relative Speed (Same direction) = V1 − V2

Distance = Speed × Time

Calculations:

⇒ Let the speed of the bus be Vb km/h.

⇒ Total relative distance to be covered by the car = 80 + 40 = 120 m.

⇒ Relative speed = (Vc − Vb) × (5/18) m/s.

⇒ Relative speed = Distance ÷ Time = 120 ÷ 15 = 8 m/s.

⇒ (75 − Vb) × (5/18) = 8

⇒ 75 − Vb = 8 × (18/5)

⇒ 75 − Vb = 144 ÷ 5

⇒ 75 − Vb = 28.8

⇒ Vb = 75 − 28.8

⇒ Vb = 46.2 km/h.

∴ The correct answer is 46.2 km/h.

Additional Information

Relative Speed Concepts

When two objects move in the same direction, relative speed = V1 − V2. When they move in opposite directions, relative speed = V1 + V2.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

General Formula

Distance = Speed × Time. In overtaking problems, the distance is the total gap closed between the two objects.

questions.question: A 1 and A 2 are two regular polygons. The sum of all the interior angles of A 1 is 1080°. Each interior angle of A 2 exceeds its exterior angle by 132°. The sum of the number of sides A 1 and A 2 is:
questions.questionHtml: A<sub>1</sub> and A<sub>2</sub> are two regular polygons. The sum of all the interior angles of A<sub>1</sub> is 1080°. Each interior angle of A<sub>2</sub> exceeds its exterior angle by 132°. The sum of the number of sides A<sub>1</sub> and A<sub>2</sub> is:
questions.solution:
The sum of all the interior angles of A1 = 1080°

⇒ (n – 2) × 180 = 1080 ⇒ (n – 2) = 6 ⇒ n = 8, so, A1 = 8

Let I is interior angle and E is the exterior angle

⇒ I – E = 132° ....(1)  [given] and I + E = 180° ....(2)   [Linear pair]

Adding equation (1) and (2)

2I = 180° + 132° ⇒ 2I = 312 ⇒ I = (312/2) ⇒ I = 156° 

Putting the value of I in equation (1), we get ⇒ 156° – E = 132° ⇒ E = 24° 

Number of sides of polygon = (360/24) ⇒ 15, so, A2 = 15

Now, the sum of the number of sides A1 and A2 = (8 + 15) ⇒ 23

questions.question: The value of \(\rm \frac{3(cosec^2 \,26^\circ-tan^2\,64^\circ)+(cot^2\,42^\circ-sec^2\,48^\circ)}{cot(22^\circ-\theta)-cosec^2(62^\circ+\theta)-tan(\theta+68^\circ)+tan^2(28^\circ-\theta)}\) is:
questions.questionHtml: The value of \(\rm \frac{3(cosec^2 \,26^\circ-tan^2\,64^\circ)+(cot^2\,42^\circ-sec^2\,48^\circ)}{cot(22^\circ-\theta)-cosec^2(62^\circ+\theta)-tan(\theta+68^\circ)+tan^2(28^\circ-\theta)}\) is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is −2
Key Points
  • To solve this expression, we utilize trigonometric identities and the properties of complementary angles where two angles sum to 90°.
  • First, let us simplify the Numerator: 3(cosec2 26° − tan2 64°) + (cot2 42° − sec2 48°).
  • Using the complementary angle rule tan(90° − A) = cot A: tan 64° = tan(90° − 26°) = cot 26°. Thus, (cosec2 26° − tan2 64°) becomes (cosec2 26° − cot2 26°). Since cosec2 A − cot2 A = 1, this term equals 1.
  • Using the rule sec(90° − A) = cosec A: sec 48° = sec(90° − 42°) = cosec 42°. Thus, (cot2 42° − sec2 48°) becomes (cot2 42° − cosec2 42°). Since cot2 A − cosec2 A = −1, this term equals −1.
  • The Numerator value is: 3(1) + (−1) = 3 − 1 = 2.
  • Next, simplify the Denominator: cot(22° − θ) − cosec2(62° + θ) − tan(θ + 68°) + tan2(28° − θ).
  • Observe that (22° − θ) and (θ + 68°) are complementary because (22 − θ) + (θ + 68) = 90°. Therefore, tan(θ + 68°) = cot(90° − (θ + 68°)) = cot(22° − θ). These two terms cancel each other out: cot(22° − θ) − cot(22° − θ) = 0.
  • Observe that (62° + θ) and (28° − θ) are complementary because (62 + θ) + (28 − θ) = 90°. Therefore, tan(28° − θ) = cot(90° − (28° − θ)) = cot(62° + θ).
  • The remaining terms in the Denominator are −cosec2(62° + θ) + cot2(62° + θ). Using the identity cot2 A − cosec2 A = −1, the denominator equals −1.
  • Finally, calculate the value of the Expression: Numerator ÷ Denominator = 2 ÷ (−1) = −2.
Additional Information
  • Fundamental Trigonometric Identities:
    • sin2 θ + cos2 θ = 1
    • 1 + tan2 θ = sec2 θ
    • 1 + cot2 θ = cosec2 θ
  • Complementary Angle Ratios:
    • sin(90° − θ) = cos θ
    • cos(90° − θ) = sin θ
    • tan(90° − θ) = cot θ
    • cot(90° − θ) = tan θ
    • sec(90° − θ) = cosec θ
    • cosec(90° − θ) = sec θ

questions.question: The average of n numbers is 45. If 60% of the numbers are increased by 5 each and the remaining numbers are decreased by 10 each, then what is the average of the numbers so obtained?
questions.questionHtml: The average of n numbers is 45. If 60% of the numbers are increased by 5 each and the remaining numbers are decreased by 10 each, then what is the average of the numbers so obtained?
questions.solution:
Let the n = 10N, 60% of n = 6N. Each of 6N number increased by 5. So, Net increase = +30N 

40% of n = 4N. Each of 4N number decreased by 10. So, Net decrease = -40N 

Net increament or decrement in sum of numbers = -40N + 30N = -10N and in average = -10N ÷ 10N = -1 

So, Required Average = 45 - 1 = 44

questions.question: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral. Sides AB and DC, when produced, meet at E and sides AD and BC when produced, meet at F. If ∠ADC = 76° and ∠AED = 55°, then ∠AFB is equal to:

questions.solution:
In ΔDAE, ∠ADC + ∠AED + ∠DAE = 180° ⇒ 76° + 55° + ∠DAE = 180° ⇒ ∠DAE = 49° 

The exterior angle of a cyclic quadrilateral is equal to the interior opposite angle ⇒ ∠DAE = ∠DCF = 49° 

Now, an exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the two interior opposite angles so, ∠ADC = ∠DCF + ∠AFB ⇒ 76° = 49° + ∠AFB ⇒ ∠AFB = 27°

questions.question: If x 2 – 3x + 1 = 0, then the value of \(\frac{(x^4+\frac{1}{x^2})}{(x^2+5x+1)}\) is:
questions.questionHtml: If x2 – 3x + 1 = 0, then the value of \(\frac{(x^4+\frac{1}{x^2})}{(x^2+5x+1)}\) is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Given x2 − 3x + 1 = 0, divide by x to get x + 1/x = 3.

Divide both numerator and denominator of the target expression by x.

Expression = (x3 + 1/x3) ÷ (x + 5 + 1/x).

Since x + 1/x = 3, then x3 + 1/x3 = 33 − 3(3) = 18.

Expression = 18 ÷ (3 + 5) = 18/8 = 9/4.

∴ The correct answer is 9/4.

Alternate Method

Given:

x2 − 3x + 1 = 0

Expression to find: (x4 + 1/x2) ÷ (x2 + 5x + 1)

Method/Formula:

If x + 1/x = k, then x3 + 1/x3 = k3 − 3k

Calculations:

⇒ x2 + 1 = 3x

⇒ (x2 + 1) ÷ x = 3x ÷ x

⇒ x + 1/x = 3

⇒ Now, divide the numerator and denominator of the expression by x:

⇒ Numerator = (x4 + 1/x2) ÷ x = x3 + 1/x3

⇒ x3 + 1/x3 = (x + 1/x)3 − 3(x + 1/x)

⇒ x3 + 1/x3 = 33 − 3 × 3 = 27 − 9 = 18

⇒ Denominator = (x2 + 5x + 1) ÷ x = x + 5 + 1/x

⇒ Denominator = (x + 1/x) + 5 = 3 + 5 = 8

⇒ Final value = 18 ÷ 8 = 9/4

∴ The correct answer is 9/4.

Additional Information

Reciprocal Sum Identities

If x + 1/x = k, then x2 + 1/x2 = k2 − 2 and x3 + 1/x3 = k3 − 3k.

Difference and Addition Relation

(x + 1/x)2 − (x − 1/x)2 = 4. This is used to find the difference of reciprocals when the sum is known.

Higher Powers

x5 + 1/x5 = (x2 + 1/x2)(x3 + 1/x3) − (x + 1/x). This formula allows solving for higher odd powers systematically.

questions.questionHtml: A and B worked together and received a total of Rs. 18,000 for 15 days. A's efficiency in the work was 5 times that of B's. The daily wage of A (in Rs.) was:
questions.solution:

questions.question: If x = 32.5, y = 34.6 and z = 30.9, then the value of x 3 + y 3 + z 3 – 3xyz is 0.98k, where k is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: If x = 32.5, y = 34.6 and z = 30.9, then the value of x<sup>3</sup> + y<sup>3</sup> + z<sup>3</sup> – 3xyz is 0.98k, where k is equal to:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Value of x3 + y3 + z3 − 3xyz = (Sum/2) × [Sum of square of differences]

Sum = 32.5 + 34.6 + 30.9 = 98

Sum of squared differences = (−2.1)2 + (3.7)2 + (−1.6)2 = 4.41 + 13.69 + 2.56 = 20.66

Expression value = 49 × 20.66 = 1012.34

k = 1012.34 ÷ 0.98 = 1033

∴ The correct answer is 1033.

Alternate Method

Given:

x = 32.5, y = 34.6, z = 30.9

Formula Used:

x3 + y3 + z3 − 3xyz = 1/2(x + y + z)[(x − y)2 + (y − z)2 + (z − x)2]

Calculations:

⇒ Sum (x + y + z) = 32.5 + 34.6 + 30.9 = 98

⇒ (x − y) = 32.5 − 34.6 = −2.1

⇒ (y − z) = 34.6 − 30.9 = 3.7

⇒ (z − x) = 30.9 − 32.5 = −1.6

⇒ x3 + y3 + z3 − 3xyz = 1/2 × 98 × [(−2.1)2 + (3.7)2 + (−1.6)2]

⇒ 0.98k = 49 × [4.41 + 13.69 + 2.56]

⇒ 0.98k = 49 × 20.66

⇒ 0.98k = 1012.34

⇒ k = 1012.34 ÷ 0.98

⇒ k = 1033

∴ The correct answer is 1033.

Additional Information

Standard Algebraic Identity

x3 + y3 + z3 − 3xyz = (x + y + z)(x2 + y2 + z2 − xy − yz − zx). This is the base form used for most expansions.

Zero Sum Property

If (x + y + z) = 0, then x3 + y3 + z3 = 3xyz. This is a very common shortcut in competitive exams.

Square Sum Variation

x3 + y3 + z3 − 3xyz = (x + y + z)[(x + y + z)2 − 3(xy + yz + zx)]. This version is useful when the sum of products is given.

questions.question: If \(\rm \frac{sec\,θ-tan\,θ}{sec\,θ+tan\,θ}=\frac{1}{7}\) , θ lies in first quadrant, then the value of \(\rm \frac{cosec\,\theta+cot^2\,\theta}{cosec\,\theta-cot^2\,\theta}\) is:
questions.questionHtml: If \(\rm \frac{sec\,θ-tan\,θ}{sec\,θ+tan\,θ}=\frac{1}{7}\), θ lies in first quadrant, then the value of \(\rm \frac{cosec\,\theta+cot^2\,\theta}{cosec\,\theta-cot^2\,\theta}\) is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

By Componendo and Dividendo: sec θ / tan θ = (7 + 1) / (7 − 1) = 8 / 6 = 4 / 3.

Since sec θ / tan θ = (1/cos θ) / (sin θ/cos θ) = 1/sin θ = cosec θ.

∴ cosec θ = 4/3 and cot2 θ = cosec2 θ − 1 = (4/3)2 − 1 = 7/9.

Required value = (4/3 + 7/9) / (4/3 − 7/9) = (19/9) / (5/9) = 19/5.

∴ The correct answer is 19/5.

Alternate Method

Given: (sec θ − tan θ) / (sec θ + tan θ) = 1/7

Formula Used: Componendo and Dividendo: If a/b = c/d, then (b+a)/(b-a) = (d+c)/(d-c). Also, cosec2 θ − cot2 θ = 1.

⇒ (sec θ − tan θ) / (sec θ + tan θ) = 1/7

⇒ [(sec θ + tan θ) + (sec θ − tan θ)] / [(sec θ + tan θ) − (sec θ − tan θ)] = (7 + 1) / (7 − 1)

⇒ (2 sec θ) / (2 tan θ) = 8 / 6

⇒ (1/cos θ) × (cos θ/sin θ) = 4 / 3

⇒ 1/sin θ = cosec θ = 4 / 3

⇒ cot2 θ = cosec2 θ − 1 = (4/3)2 − 1 = 16/9 − 1 = 7/9

⇒ Value = (cosec θ + cot2 θ) / (cosec θ − cot2 θ)

⇒ Value = (4/3 + 7/9) / (4/3 − 7/9)

⇒ Value = [(12 + 7) / 9] / [(12 − 7) / 9] = 19 / 5

∴ The correct answer is 19/5.

Additional Information

Componendo and Dividendo Rule

If the ratio a/b = c/d, then (a + b) / (a − b) = (c + d) / (c − d). This is very useful in simplifying trigonometric fractions.

Trigonometric Identities

The three fundamental identities are: sin2 θ + cos2 θ = 1, sec2 θ − tan2 θ = 1, and cosec2 θ − cot2 θ = 1.

Quadrant Rule for Trigonometry

In the first quadrant (0 ° to 90 °), all trigonometric ratios (sin, cos, tan, cosec, sec, cot) are positive.

questions.question: The sum of the digits of the least number which when divided by 36, 72, 80 and 88 leaves the remainders 16, 52, 60 and 68, respectively, is:
questions.questionHtml: The sum of the digits of the least number which when divided by 36, 72, 80 and 88 leaves the remainders 16, 52, 60 and 68, respectively, is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Find the common difference (k): (36 − 16) = (72 − 52) = (80 − 60) = (88 − 68) = 20.

The least number is LCM(36, 72, 80, 88) − k.

LCM(36, 72, 80, 88) = 7920.

Required Number = 7920 − 20 = 7900.

Sum of digits = 7 + 9 + 0 + 0 = 16.

∴ The correct answer is 16.

Alternate Method

Given divisors and their respective remainders:

To find the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of 36, 72, 80, and 88:

⇒ Prime factorisation:

⇒ 36 = 22 × 32

⇒ 72 = 23 × 32

⇒ 80 = 24 × 5

⇒ 88 = 23 × 11

⇒ LCM = 24 × 32 × 5 × 11

⇒ LCM = 16 × 9 × 5 × 11 = 7920

⇒ The least number (N) = LCM − Common Difference

⇒ N = 7920 − 20 = 7900

⇒ Sum of digits of N = 7 + 9 + 0 + 0 = 16

∴ The correct answer is 16.

Additional Information

LCM with Constant Difference

When a number leaves remainders r1, r2, r3 when divided by a, b, c such that (a−r1) = (b−r2) = (c−r3) = k, the number is LCM(a, b, c) − k.

LCM with Same Remainder

If the number leaves the same remainder 'r' in each case when divided by a, b, c, then the least such number is LCM(a, b, c) + r.

Divisibility of Sum of Digits

If the sum of digits of a number is divisible by 3 or 9, then the number itself is divisible by 3 or 9 respectively.

questions.question: The expression (tan θ + cot θ) (sec θ + tan θ) (1 – sin θ), 0° < θ < 90°, is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: The expression (tan θ + cot θ) (sec θ + tan θ) (1 – sin θ), 0° < θ < 90°, is equal to:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Use the value substitution method by picking a specific angle, let θ = 30°.

Substitute values: tan 30° = 1/√3, cot 30° = √3, sec 30° = 2/√3, sin 30° = 1/2.

Expression = (1/√3 + √3) × (2/√3 + 1/√3) × (1 − 1/2) = (4/√3) × (3/√3) × (1/2).

Expression = (4/√3) × √3 × 1/2 = 2.

Check options for θ = 30°: cosec 30° = 1/sin 30° = 1/(1/2) = 2.

∴ The correct answer is cosec θ.

Alternate Method

Given: The expression (tan θ + cot θ) (sec θ + tan θ) (1 − sin θ) for 0° < θ < 90°.

Formula Used: tan θ = sin θ/cos θ; cot θ = cos θ/sin θ; sec θ = 1/cos θ; sin2θ + cos2θ = 1.

⇒ Simplifying (tan θ + cot θ) = (sin θ / cos θ + cos θ / sin θ) = (sin2θ + cos2θ) / (sin θ cos θ)

⇒ (tan θ + cot θ) = 1 / (sin θ cos θ)

⇒ Simplifying (sec θ + tan θ)(1 − sin θ) = (1/cos θ + sin θ/cos θ)(1 − sin θ)

⇒ ((1 + sin θ) / cos θ) × (1 − sin θ) = (1 − sin2θ) / cos θ

⇒ cos2θ / cos θ = cos θ

⇒ Multiplying both parts: [1 / (sin θ cos θ)] × cos θ = 1 / sin θ

⇒ 1 / sin θ = cosec θ

∴ The correct answer is cosec θ.

Additional Information

Reciprocal Identities

Trigonometric ratios are related by reciprocals: cosec θ = 1/sin θ, sec θ = 1/cos θ, and cot θ = 1/tan θ.

Pythagorean Identities

Fundamental identities include sin2θ + cos2θ = 1, 1 + tan2θ = sec2θ, and 1 + cot2θ = cosec2θ.

Quotient Identities

The tangent and cotangent functions can be expressed as ratios: tan θ = sin θ/cos θ and cot θ = cos θ/sin θ.

\(9 \div [\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{6}\div(\frac{3}{4}-\frac{1}{3})\;of\;\frac{2}{9}]\)

Formula used:

BODMAS rule (Bracket, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction)

Calculation:

⇒ \(9 \div [\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{6} \div (\frac{9-4}{12})\;of\;\frac{2}{9}]\)

⇒ \(9 \div [\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{6} \div \frac{5}{12}\;of\;\frac{2}{9}]\)

⇒ \(9 \div [\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{6} \div (\frac{5}{12} \times \frac{2}{9})]\)

⇒ \(9 \div [\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{6} \div \frac{5}{54}]\)

⇒ \(9 \div [\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{6} \times \frac{54}{5}]\)

⇒ \(9 \div [\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{4} + \frac{9}{5}]\)

⇒ \(9 \div [\frac{30 + 20 + 15 + 108}{60}]\)

⇒ \(9 \div \frac{173}{60}\)

⇒ \(9 \times \frac{60}{173}\)

⇒ \(\frac{540}{173}\)

questions.question: A well with inner radius 3 m, is dug 6 m deep. The soil taken out of it has been spread evenly all around it to a width of 2 m to form an embankment. The height (in m) of the embankment is:
questions.questionHtml: A well with inner radius 3 m, is dug 6 m deep. The soil taken out of it has been spread evenly all around it to a width of 2 m to form an embankment. The height (in m) of the embankment is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Inner radius (r) = 3 m, Depth (h) = 6 m, Embankment Width = 2 m

Outer radius (R) = r + width = 3 + 2 = 5 m

Height of embankment (H) = (r2 × h) / (R2 − r2)

H = (32 × 6) / (52 − 32)

H = 54 / (25 − 9) = 54 / 16 = 27 / 8 = 3 3/8 m

∴ The correct answer is 3 3/8 m.

Alternate Method

Given:

Inner radius of well (r) = 3 m

Depth of well (h) = 6 m

Width of embankment = 2 m

Formula Used:

Volume of Cylinder = π × r2 × h

Volume of Embankment (Hollow Cylinder) = π × (R2 − r2) × H

Calculations:

⇒ Volume of soil taken out = π × r2 × h

⇒ Volume of soil = π × 32 × 6 = 54π m3

⇒ Outer radius of embankment (R) = Inner radius + width = 3 + 2 = 5 m

⇒ Volume of embankment = π × (R2 − r2) × H

⇒ Volume of embankment = π × (52 − 32) × H = π × (25 − 9) × H = 16πH

⇒ Volume of soil = Volume of embankment

⇒ 54π = 16πH

⇒ H = 54 / 16 = 27 / 8

⇒ H = 3 3/8 m

∴ The correct answer is 3 3/8 m.

Additional Information

Volume of Cylinder

The volume of a solid cylinder is given by V = πr2h, where r is the radius and h is the height.

Volume of Hollow Cylinder (Embankment)

The volume of a hollow cylinder is the difference between the volumes of the outer and inner cylinders: V = π(R2 − r2)h.

Conservation of Volume

When an object is reshaped (like soil from a hole used to build a platform), the total volume remains constant.

questions.question: The expression \(\rm \frac{tan^6 \,θ-sec^6\,θ+3sec^2\,θ \,tan^2\,θ}{tan^2\,θ+cot^2\,θ+2}\) , 0° < θ < 90°, is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: The expression \(\rm \frac{tan^6 \,θ-sec^6\,θ+3sec^2\,θ \,tan^2\,θ}{tan^2\,θ+cot^2\,θ+2}\), 0° < θ < 90°, is equal to:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Substitute θ = 45° where tan 45° = 1, cot 45° = 1, and sec 45° = √2.

Numerator = 16 − (√2)6 + 3(√2)2(1)2 = 1 − 8 + 3(2) = 1 − 8 + 6 = −1.

Denominator = 12 + 12 + 2 = 1 + 1 + 2 = 4.

Simplified value = −1/4. Checking Option 4: −cos245° sin245° = −(1/2) × (1/2) = −1/4.

∴ The correct answer is −cos2 θ sin2 θ.

Alternate Method

Given: expression = (tan6 θ − sec6 θ + 3sec2 θ tan2 θ) ÷ (tan2 θ + cot2 θ + 2)

Formula Used: (a − b)3 = a3 − b3 − 3ab(a − b); sec2 θ − tan2 θ = 1; sin2 θ + cos2 θ = 1

⇒ Let x = tan2 θ and y = sec2 θ. We know x − y = −1.

⇒ Numerator = x3 − y3 + 3xy = x3 − y3 − 3xy(−1)

⇒ Substituting (−1) with (x − y): Numerator = x3 − y3 − 3xy(x − y) = (x − y)3

⇒ Numerator = (−1)3 = −1

⇒ Denominator = tan2 θ + cot2 θ + 2 = (tan θ + cot θ)2

⇒ Denominator = (sin θ ÷ cos θ + cos θ ÷ sin θ)2 = [(sin2 θ + cos2 θ) ÷ (sin θ cos θ)]2

⇒ Since sin2 θ + cos2 θ = 1, Denominator = [1 ÷ (sin θ cos θ)]2 = 1 ÷ (sin2 θ cos2 θ)

⇒ Final Expression = −1 ÷ [1 ÷ (sin2 θ cos2 θ)] = −sin2 θ cos2 θ

∴ The correct answer is −cos2 θ sin2 θ.

Additional Information

Pythagorean Identities

Fundamental relations used: sin2 θ + cos2 θ = 1, sec2 θ − tan2 θ = 1, and cosec2 θ − cot2 θ = 1.

Reciprocal and Quotient Relations

tan θ + cot θ = sec θ cosec θ = 1 ÷ (sin θ cos θ), which is a common simplification for sum of squares.

Algebraic Cube Identity

The form a3 ± b3 ± 3ab(a ± b) = (a ± b)3 is frequently used to simplify high-power trigonometric expressions.

questions.question: An athlete runs 8 times around a circular field of radius 7 m in 3 minutes 40 seconds. His speed (in km/h) is: (Take π = \(\frac{22}{7}\) )
questions.questionHtml:
An athlete runs 8 times around a circular field of radius 7 m in 3 minutes 40 seconds. His speed (in km/h) is:

(Take π = \(\frac{22}{7}\))
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For radius r = 7 m, Circumference = 44 m.

Total distance for 8 rounds = 8 × 44 = 352 m.

Total time in seconds = (3 × 60) + 40 = 220 s.

Speed = (352 ÷ 220) × (18 ÷ 5) = 1.6 × 3.6 = 144/25 km/h.

∴ The correct answer is 144/25 km/h.

Alternate Method

Given:

Radius of circular field (r) = 7 m

Number of rounds (n) = 8

Time (t) = 3 minutes 40 seconds

Formula:

Circumference of circle = 2 × π × r

Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Calculations:

⇒ Circumference (C) = 2 × (22 ÷ 7) × 7 = 44 m

⇒ Total Distance (D) = 8 × 44 = 352 m

⇒ Total Time (t) in seconds = (3 × 60) + 40 = 220 s

⇒ Speed (v) in m/s = 352 ÷ 220 = 1.6 m/s

⇒ Speed in km/h = 1.6 × (18 ÷ 5)

⇒ Speed = (16 ÷ 10) × (18 ÷ 5) = (8 ÷ 5) × (18 ÷ 5)

⇒ Speed = 144 ÷ 25 km/h

∴ The correct answer is 144/25 km/h.

Additional Information

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from m/s to km/h, multiply the value by 18/5. Conversely, multiply by 5/18 to convert km/h to m/s.

Distance in Circular Motion

The total distance covered in n rounds around a circular path is n × (2πr), where r is the radius of the circle.

Average Speed

Average speed is defined as the total distance traveled divided by the total time taken (Total Distance ÷ Total Time).

questions.question: Three numbers are in the ratio \(\frac{1}{2} : \frac{2}{3} : \frac{3}{4}\) . If the difference between the greatest number and the smallest number is 33, then HCF of the three numbers is:
questions.questionHtml: Three numbers are in the ratio \(\frac{1}{2} : \frac{2}{3} : \frac{3}{4}\). If the difference between the greatest number and the smallest number is 33, then HCF of the three numbers is:

 A : B : C = 12 × (1/2) : 12 × (2/3) : 12 × (3/4) = 6 : 8 : 9

C - A = 9x - 6x = 33 ⇒ x = 11 

Now, the number is 6 × 11, 8 × 11 and 9 × 11

∴ The highest common factor (HCF) is 11 in these three numbers

questions.question: In a square ABCD, diagonals AC and BD intersect at O. The angle bisector of ∠CAB meets BD and BC at F and G, respectively. OF ∶ CG is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: In a square ABCD, diagonals AC and BD intersect at O. The angle bisector of ∠CAB meets BD and BC at F and G, respectively. OF ∶ CG is equal to:
questions.solution:
Let the side AB be x, so, Diagonal AC = √2.x

⇒ OA = OB = OC = OD = AC/2 = x/√2    ----(i)

In ΔAOB and from angle bisector theorem  AB : AO = BF : OF ⇒ x : (x/√2)  = BF/OF ⇒ √2 : 1 = BF/OF

Let BF = √2y, OF = y      ----(ii)

Since, BF + OF = OB = x/√2 ⇒ √2y + y = x/√2 ⇒ y = \(OF = \frac{x}{\sqrt2 . (\sqrt2 + 1)}\)    ----(iii) 

Now, In ΔABC and from angle bisector theorem, AB : AC = BG : GC ⇒ x : √2x  = BG : GC ⇒ 1 : √2 = BG : GC

Let BG = z, GC = √2z      ----(iv)

Since, BG + GC = BC = x ⇒ z + √2z = x ⇒ \(z = \frac{x}{(\sqrt2 + 1)}\) ⇒ \(\sqrt2.z = \frac{\sqrt2x}{(\sqrt2 + 1)}\) ⇒ \(CG = \frac{\sqrt2x}{(\sqrt2 + 1)}\)      ----(v)

Now from (iii) and (v), we get 

OF : CG = \( \frac{x}{\sqrt2 . (\sqrt2 + 1)} : \frac{\sqrt2x}{(\sqrt2 + 1)}\) ⇒ OF : CG = \( \frac{1}{\sqrt2} : \frac{\sqrt2}{1}\) ⇒ OF : CG = 1 : 2

questions.question: The distance between two places A and B is 140 km. Two cars x and y start simultaneously from A and B, respectively. If they move in the same direction, they meet after 7 hours. If they move towards each other, they meet after one hour. What is the speed (in km/h) of car y if its speed is more than that of car x?
questions.questionHtml: The distance between two places A and B is 140 km. Two cars x and y start simultaneously from A and B, respectively. If they move in the same direction, they meet after 7 hours. If they move towards each other, they meet after one hour. What is the speed (in km/h) of car y if its speed is more than that of car x?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Relative speed in same direction = Total Distance ÷ Time = 140 ÷ 7 = 20 km/h

Relative speed in opposite direction = Total Distance ÷ Time = 140 ÷ 1 = 140 km/h

Speed of faster car (y) = (Sum of relative speeds + Difference of relative speeds) ÷ 2

Sy = (140 + 20) ÷ 2 = 160 ÷ 2 = 80 km/h

∴ The correct answer is 80 km/h.

Alternate Method

Given:

Distance (D) = 140 km

Time taken in same direction (t1) = 7 hours

Time taken in opposite direction (t2) = 1 hour

Condition: Speed of y (Sy) > Speed of x (Sx)

Formula Used:

Relative speed (Opposite direction) = S1 + S2

Relative speed (Same direction) = S1 − S2 (where S1 > S2)

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Calculations:

⇒ Case 1 (Opposite direction): Sy + Sx = 140 ÷ 1

⇒ Sy + Sx = 140 — (Equation 1)

⇒ Case 2 (Same direction): Sy − Sx = 140 ÷ 7

⇒ Sy − Sx = 20 — (Equation 2)

Adding Equation 1 and Equation 2:

⇒ (Sy + Sx) + (Sy − Sx) = 140 + 20

⇒ 2Sy = 160

⇒ Sy = 160 ÷ 2 = 80 km/h

Substituting Sy in Equation 1:

⇒ 80 + Sx = 140

⇒ Sx = 140 − 80 = 60 km/h

Checking condition: Sy (80) > Sx (60). Condition satisfied.

∴ The correct answer is 80 km/h.

Additional Information

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference (u − v). When they move in opposite directions, it is the sum (u + v).

Speed Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Average Speed for Constant Distance

If an object covers the same distance at speed u and then at speed v, the average speed is (2 × u × v) ÷ (u + v).

questions.question: The monthly salary of a person was Rs. 1,60,000. He used to spend on three heads — Personal and family expenses (P), Taxes (T) and Education loan (E). The rest were his savings. P was 50% of the income. E was 20% of P, and T was 15% of E. When his salary got raised by 30%, he maintained the percentage level of P, but E became 30% of P and T became 20% of E. The sum of the two savings (in Rs.) is:
questions.questionHtml: The monthly salary of a person was Rs. 1,60,000. He used to spend on three heads — Personal and family expenses (P), Taxes (T) and Education loan (E). The rest were his savings. P was 50% of the income. E was 20% of P, and T was 15% of E. When his salary got raised by 30%, he maintained the percentage level of P, but E became 30% of P and T became 20% of E. The sum of the two savings (in Rs.) is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Savings % (Old) = 100% − [50% + (20% of 50%) + (15% of 10%)] = 100% − 61.5% = 38.5%

Savings 1 = 38.5% of 1,60,000 = ₹61,600

New Salary = 1.30 × 1,60,000 = ₹2,08,000

Savings % (New) = 100% − [50% + (30% of 50%) + (20% of 15%)] = 100% − 68% = 32%

Savings 2 = 32% of 2,08,000 = ₹66,560

Total Savings = 61,600 + 66,560 = ₹1,28,160

∴ The correct answer is ₹1,28,160.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial Salary = ₹1,60,000

Expenses: P = 50% of Income, E = 20% of P, T = 15% of E

New Salary = Initial × 130%

New Expenses: P = 50% of Income, E = 30% of P, T = 20% of E

Step 1: Calculate Initial Savings

⇒ P1 = 50% of 1,60,000 = ₹80,000

⇒ E1 = 20% of 80,000 = ₹16,000

⇒ T1 = 15% of 16,000 = ₹2,400

⇒ Savings1 = 1,60,000 − (80,000 + 16,000 + 2,400) = ₹61,600

Step 2: Calculate New Savings after 30% Raise

⇒ New Salary = 1,60,000 × 1.3 = ₹2,08,000

⇒ P2 = 50% of 2,08,000 = ₹1,04,000

⇒ E2 = 30% of 1,04,000 = ₹31,200

⇒ T2 = 20% of 31,200 = ₹6,240

⇒ Savings2 = 2,08,000 − (1,04,000 + 31,200 + 6,240) = ₹66,560

Step 3: Calculate the Sum

⇒ Total Savings = 61,600 + 66,560 = ₹1,28,160

∴ The correct answer is ₹1,28,160.

Additional Information

Percentage of Percentage

When a value is a percentage of another percentage, multiply the decimals: x% of y% of Total = (x/100) × (y/100) × Total.

Successive Increment

A salary raise of r% is calculated as: New Salary = Original Salary × (1 + r/100).

Savings Calculation

Savings = Total Income − Sum of all individual expenses (P + E + T + ...).

questions.question: The radius of a spherical balloon is inflated from 7 cm to 10.5 cm. The percentage increase in its surface area is:
questions.questionHtml: The radius of a spherical balloon is inflated from 7 cm to 10.5 cm. The percentage increase in its surface area is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of radii (r1 : r2) = 7 : 10.5 = 2 : 3

Surface area of sphere is proportional to r2

Ratio of surface areas (A1 : A2) = 22 : 32 = 4 : 9

Increase in units = 9 − 4 = 5

Percentage increase = (Increase ÷ Original value) × 100 = (5 ÷ 4) × 100 = 125%

∴ The correct answer is 125%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial radius (r1) = 7 cm

Final radius (r2) = 10.5 cm

Formula Used:

Surface area of a sphere = 4 × π × r2

Percentage increase = [(New Area − Old Area) ÷ Old Area] × 100

Calculations:

⇒ Initial Surface Area (S1) = 4 × π × (7)2 = 196π cm2

⇒ Final Surface Area (S2) = 4 × π × (10.5)2 = 4 × π × 110.25 = 441π cm2

⇒ Increase in Surface Area = 441π − 196π = 245π cm2

⇒ Percentage Increase = (245π ÷ 196π) × 100

⇒ Percentage Increase = (245 ÷ 196) × 100

⇒ Percentage Increase = (5 ÷ 4) × 100

⇒ Percentage Increase = 1.25 × 100 = 125%

∴ The correct answer is 125%.

Additional Information

Volume of a Sphere

The volume (V) is given by (4/3) × π × r3. If radius increases in ratio a:b, volume increases in ratio a3:b3.

Hemisphere Surface Areas

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2 × π × r2 and Total Surface Area (TSA) = 3 × π × r2.

Scaling Factor Rule

For any 3D object, if linear dimensions are scaled by factor 'k', area scales by k2 and volume scales by k3.

questions.question: The volume of a cylinder is 4312 cm 3 . Its curved surface area is one-third of its total surface area. Its curved surface area (in cm 2 ) is: (Take π = \(\frac{22}{7}\) )
questions.questionHtml:
The volume of a cylinder is 4312 cm3. Its curved surface area is one-third of its total surface area. Its curved surface area (in cm2) is:

(Take π = \(\frac{22}{7}\))
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio CSA/TSA = 1/3 ⇒ 2πrh / [2πr(h+r)] = 1/3 ⇒ h/(h+r) = 1/3 ⇒ r = 2h.

Volume = πr2h = π(2h)2h = 4πh3 = 4312.

4 × (22/7) × h3 = 4312 ⇒ h3 = 343 ⇒ h = 7 cm.

Radius r = 2 × 7 = 14 cm.

CSA = 2 × (22/7) × 14 × 7 = 616 cm2.

∴ The correct answer is 616 cm2.

Alternate Method

Given: Volume = 4312 cm3, Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 1/3 Total Surface Area (TSA).

Formula Used: Volume = πr2h; CSA = 2πrh; TSA = 2πr(h+r).

⇒ CSA = 1/3 TSA

⇒ 2πrh = 1/3 [2πr(h + r)]

⇒ 3h = h + r ⇒ r = 2h

⇒ Volume = πr2h = 4312

⇒ (22/7) × (2h)2 × h = 4312

⇒ (22/7) × 4h3 = 4312

⇒ h3 = (4312 × 7) / 88

⇒ h3 = 343 ⇒ h = 7 cm

⇒ r = 2 × 7 = 14 cm

⇒ CSA = 2 × (22/7) × 14 × 7 = 616

∴ The correct answer is 616 cm2.

Additional Information

Volume of Cylinder

It is the capacity of the cylinder, calculated as Base Area × Height, V = πr2h.

Surface Areas of Cylinder

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2πrh. Total Surface Area (TSA) includes the two circular bases, TSA = 2πrh + 2πr2.

Special Case: CSA = 1/2 TSA

If CSA is half of TSA, then 2πrh = 2πr2, which means the height of the cylinder is equal to its radius (h = r).

questions.question: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 12 minutes and 24 minutes, respectively, while a third pipe C can empty the full tank in 32 minutes. All the three pipes are opened simultaneously. However, pipe C is closed 2 minutes before the tank is filled. In how much time (in minutes) will the tank be full?
questions.questionHtml: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 12 minutes and 24 minutes, respectively, while a third pipe C can empty the full tank in 32 minutes. All the three pipes are opened simultaneously. However, pipe C is closed 2 minutes before the tank is filled. In how much time (in minutes) will the tank be full?
questions.solution:
Let the capacity of tank be 96 unit   [LCM of 12, 24, 32]

Efficiency of pipe A = 96 ÷ 12 = 8 unit/min

Efficiency of pipe B = 96 ÷ 24 = 4 unit/min

Efficiency of pipe C = 96 ÷ 32 = -3 unit/min

Combined efficiency of A + B + C = 9 unit/min 

Let if C is not closed 2 min before then 

Work done by C in 2 min = 2 × -3 = -6 unit 

So, Total work done by all pipes = 96 + (-6) = 90 unit 

So, Required time = 90 ÷ 9 = 10 min

questions.question: A solid metallic sphere of radius 4 cm is melted and recast into spheres of the radius of 2 cm each. What is the ratio of the surface area of the original sphere to the sum of surface area of the spheres, so formed?
questions.questionHtml: A solid metallic sphere of radius 4 cm is melted and recast into spheres of the radius of 2 cm each. What is the ratio of the surface area of the original sphere to the sum of surface area of the spheres, so formed?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Number of spheres (n) = (Original Radius ÷ New Radius)3 = (4 ÷ 2)3 = 23 = 8

Surface Area Ratio = Original Area : (n × New Area)

Ratio = R2 : (n × r2) = 42 : (8 × 22) = 16 : (8 × 4)

Ratio = 16 : 32 = 1 : 2

∴ The correct answer is 1 : 2.

Alternate Method

Given:

Radius of original sphere (R) = 4 cm

Radius of small sphere (r) = 2 cm

Formula Used:

Volume of sphere = (4/3) × π × radius3

Surface area of sphere = 4 × π × radius2

Calculations:

⇒ Total volume remains constant during melting.

⇒ Volume of original sphere = n × Volume of small sphere

⇒ (4/3) × π × 43 = n × (4/3) × π × 23

⇒ 64 = n × 8

⇒ n = 8

⇒ Surface area of original sphere (SA1) = 4 × π × 42 = 64π cm2

⇒ Sum of surface areas of 8 small spheres (SAtotal) = 8 × (4 × π × 22)

⇒ SAtotal = 8 × 16π = 128π cm2

⇒ Required Ratio = SA1 : SAtotal = 64π : 128π

⇒ Ratio = 1 : 2

∴ The correct answer is 1 : 2.

Additional Information

Conservation of Volume

When a solid is melted and recast into other shapes, the total volume remains constant (Vinitial = Vfinal).

Sphere Properties

For a sphere of radius R: Volume = (4/3)πR3 and Total Surface Area = 4πR2.

Ratio of Dimensions

If the ratio of radii of two spheres is a:b, then the ratio of their surface areas is a2:b2 and the ratio of their volumes is a3:b3.

questions.question: Two circles of radius 13 cm and 15 cm intersect each other at points A and B. If the length of the common chord is 24 cm, then what is the distance between their centres?
questions.questionHtml: Two circles of radius 13 cm and 15 cm intersect each other at points A and B. If the length of the common chord is 24 cm, then what is the distance between their centres?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Line joining centers bisects the common chord perpendicularly.

Half of the common chord = 24 ÷ 2 = 12 cm.

Using Pythagorean triplet (5, 12, 13): Distance 1 = 5 cm.

Using Pythagorean triplet (9, 12, 15): Distance 2 = 9 cm.

Distance between centers = 5 + 9 = 14 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 14 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Radius of circle 1 (O₁) = 13 cm

Radius of circle 2 (O₂) = 15 cm

Length of common chord (AB) = 24 cm

Formula Used:

Perpendicular from centre bisects the chord

O₁M = √(r₁2 − AM2)

O₂M = √(r₂2 − AM2)

O₁O₂ = O₁M + O₂M

Calculation:

AM = AB/2 = 24/2 = 12 cm

In △O₁MA,

⇒ O₁M = √(132 − 122)

⇒ O₁M = √(169 − 144)

⇒ O₁M = √25 = 5 cm

In △O₂MA,

⇒ O₂M = √(152 − 122)

⇒ O₂M = √(225 − 144)

⇒ O₂M = √81 = 9 cm

⇒ O₁O₂ = O₁M + O₂M = 5 + 9 = 14 cm

∴ The distance between the centres is 14 cm.

Additional Information

Common Chord Property

The line joining the centers of two intersecting circles is the perpendicular bisector of the common chord.

Length of Common Chord

Pythagorean Triplets

Sets like (3,4,5), (5,12,13), (7,24,25), and (8,15,17) help solve geometry problems involving right triangles quickly.

questions.question: By selling an article for Rs. 2,200, a profit of 10% is earned. If the same article is sold for Rs. 2,600, then what will be the gain percentage?
questions.questionHtml: By selling an article for Rs. 2,200, a profit of 10% is earned. If the same article is sold for Rs. 2,600, then what will be the gain percentage?
questions.solution:
SP = Rs.2200 and Profit = 10%  = (1/10)

Then CP = 10 and SP = 10 + 1 = 11 

Here, 11 unit → 2200, then CP = 10 unit → 2200/11 × 10 = 2000

New SP = Rs.2600, so new profit = (2600 - 2000) = 600

New profit% = 600/2000 × 100 ⇒ 30%

questions.question: A dealer offers a cash discount of 20% and still makes a profit of 20%. If he further sells 8 articles at a rate of 6 articles, then how much percentage above the cost price does he mark on each article?
questions.questionHtml: A dealer offers a cash discount of 20% and still makes a profit of 20%. If he further sells 8 articles at a rate of 6 articles, then how much percentage above the cost price does he mark on each article?
questions.solution:
Let MP = 100, so, SP = 80

SP = CP × (100 + Profit)/100 ⇒ 80 = CP × (100 + 20)/100

⇒ CP = 8000/120 ⇒ CP = 200/3

He sells 8 articles at a rate of 6 articles, then for 8 articles, CP = 6 × 200/3 = 400

CP of 8 Articles = 400, then CP of one article = 400/8 = 50

So, The % marked above the cost price ⇒ [(MP - CP)/CP] × 100

⇒ [(100 - 50)/50] × 100 ⇒ 100 %

questions.question: If 27x 3 – 64y 3 = (Ax + By) (Cx 2 – Dy 2 + 12xy), then the value of 4A + B + 3C + 2D is:
questions.questionHtml: If 27x<sup>3</sup> – 64y<sup>3</sup> = (Ax + By) (Cx<sup>2</sup> – Dy<sup>2</sup> + 12xy), then the value of 4A + B + 3C + 2D is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Use the algebraic identity: a3 − b3 = (a − b)(a2 + ab + b2)

Here, 27x3 − 64y3 = (3x)3 − (4y)3 = (3x − 4y)(9x2 + 12xy + 16y2)

Comparing with (Ax + By)(Cx2 − Dy2 + 12xy), we get:

A = 3, B = −4, C = 9, D = −16

Value = 4(3) + (−4) + 3(9) + 2(−16) = 12 − 4 + 27 − 32 = 3

∴ The correct answer is 3.

Alternate Method

Given: 27x3 − 64y3 = (Ax + By) (Cx2 − Dy2 + 12xy)

Formula: a3 − b3 = (a − b)(a2 + ab + b2)

⇒ 27x3 − 64y3 = (3x)3 − (4y)3

⇒ (3x − 4y)((3x)2 + (3x)(4y) + (4y)2)

⇒ (3x − 4y)(9x2 + 12xy + 16y2)

⇒ By comparing the coefficients with (Ax + By)(Cx2 − Dy2 + 12xy):

⇒ A = 3, B = −4, C = 9

⇒ −Dy2 = 16y2 ⇒ D = −16

⇒ Target expression = 4A + B + 3C + 2D

⇒ 4(3) + (−4) + 3(9) + 2(−16)

⇒ 12 − 4 + 27 − 32

⇒ 35 − 32 = 3

∴ The correct answer is 3.

Additional Information

Sum of Cubes Identity

The sum of cubes is given by a3 + b3 = (a + b)(a2 − ab + b2).

Square of a Binomial

The square identities are (a + b)2 = a2 + 2ab + b2 and (a − b)2 = a2 − 2ab + b2.

Identity for (a + b + c)2

The square of a trinomial is (a + b + c)2 = a2 + b2 + c2 + 2(ab + bc + ca).

questions.question: The expression \(\rm \frac{cos^4 \,θ-sin^4\,θ+2sin^2\,θ+3}{(cosec\,θ+cot\,θ+1)(cosec\,θ-cot\,θ+1)-2}\) , 0° < θ < 90°, is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: The expression \(\rm \frac{cos^4 \,θ-sin^4\,θ+2sin^2\,θ+3}{(cosec\,θ+cot\,θ+1)(cosec\,θ-cot\,θ+1)-2}\), 0° < θ < 90°, is equal to:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Pick a standard angle θ = 30° where 0° < θ < 90°.

Numerator = (cos 30°)4 − (sin 30°)4 + 2(sin 30°)2 + 3 = (9/16) − (1/16) + 2(1/4) + 3 = 4.

Denominator = (cosec 30° + cot 30° + 1)(cosec 30° − cot 30° + 1) − 2 = (2 + √3 + 1)(2 − √3 + 1) − 2 = (3 + √3)(3 − √3) − 2 = 9 − 3 − 2 = 4.

Expression Value = 4 ÷ 4 = 1. Matching options: (2) 2 sin 30° = 2 × 1/2 = 1.

∴ The correct answer is 2sin θ.

Alternate Method

Given: [(cos4θ − sin4θ) + 2sin2θ + 3] ÷ [(cosecθ + cotθ + 1)(cosecθ − cotθ + 1) − 2]

Formula Used: a2 − b2 = (a − b)(a + b); cosec2θ − cot2θ = 1; sin2θ + cos2θ = 1.

Step 1: Simplify the Numerator

⇒ cos4θ − sin4θ = (cos2θ − sin2θ)(cos2θ + sin2θ) = (cos2θ − sin2θ) × 1

⇒ Numerator = (cos2θ − sin2θ) + 2sin2θ + 3

⇒ Numerator = cos2θ + sin2θ + 3 = 1 + 3 = 4

Step 2: Simplify the Denominator

⇒ [(cosecθ + 1) + cotθ][(cosecθ + 1) − cotθ] − 2

⇒ (cosecθ + 1)2 − cot2θ − 2

⇒ (cosec2θ + 2cosecθ + 1) − cot2θ − 2

⇒ (cosec2θ − cot2θ) + 2cosecθ + 1 − 2

⇒ 1 + 2cosecθ − 1 = 2cosecθ

Step 3: Calculate the Final Expression

⇒ Expression = 4 ÷ (2cosecθ) = 2 × (1 ÷ cosecθ)

⇒ Expression = 2sin θ

∴ The correct answer is 2sin θ.

Additional Information

Fundamental Identities

Standard identities like sin2θ + cos2θ = 1, 1 + tan2θ = sec2θ, and 1 + cot2θ = cosec2θ are used to reduce complex power terms.

Algebraic Forms in Trigonometry

Expressions of type x4 − y4 can always be factored into (x2 − y2)(x2 + y2), which often simplifies to a lower degree using identities.

Value Substitution Trick

If an expression is true for all θ within a range, substitute simple angles like 30°, 45°, or 60° to find the numeric result and match with options.

questions.question: The expression \(\rm \frac{(1-sin\,θ+cos\,θ)^2(1-cos\,θ)sec^3\,θ cosec^2\,θ}{(sec\,θ -tan\,θ)(tan\,θ+cot\,θ)} \) , 0° < θ < 90°, is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: The expression \(\rm \frac{(1-sin\,θ+cos\,θ)^2(1-cos\,θ)sec^3\,θ cosec^2\,θ}{(sec\,θ -tan\,θ)(tan\,θ+cot\,θ)} \), 0° < θ < 90°, is equal to:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Substitute θ = 45° into the expression.

Numerator = (1 − 1/√2 + 1/√2)2 × (1 − 1/√2) × (√2)3 × (√2)2 = 1 × (1 − 1/√2) × 2√2 × 2 = 4√2 − 4

Denominator = (√2 − 1) × (1 + 1) = 2(√2 − 1) = 2√2 − 2

Expression Value = (4√2 − 4) ÷ (2√2 − 2) = 2

Checking options: 2 tan 45° = 2 × 1 = 2.

∴ The correct answer is 2 tan θ.

Alternate Method

Given: Expression = [(1 − sin θ + cos θ)2 (1 − cos θ) sec3 θ csc2 θ] / [(sec θ − tan θ)(tan θ + cot θ)]

Simplify the components step by step:

⇒ (1 − sin θ + cos θ)2 = 1 + sin2 θ + cos2 θ − 2sin θ + 2cos θ − 2sin θcos θ

⇒ 2 − 2sin θ + 2cos θ − 2sin θcos θ = 2(1 − sin θ) + 2cos θ(1 − sin θ) = 2(1 − sin θ)(1 + cos θ)

⇒ Numerator = 2(1 − sin θ)(1 + cos θ)(1 − cos θ) (1/cos3 θ) (1/sin2 θ)

⇒ 2(1 − sin θ)(1 − cos2 θ) / (cos3 θ sin2 θ) = 2(1 − sin θ)sin2 θ / (cos3 θ sin2 θ) = 2(1 − sin θ) / cos3 θ

⇒ Denominator = [(1 − sin θ) / cos θ] × [sin θ / cos θ + cos θ / sin θ]

⇒ [(1 − sin θ) / cos θ] × [(sin2 θ + cos2 θ) / (sin θ cos θ)] = (1 − sin θ) / (sin θ cos2 θ)

⇒ Final Ratio = [2(1 − sin θ) / cos3 θ] ÷ [(1 − sin θ) / (sin θ cos2 θ)]

⇒ [2(1 − sin θ) / cos3 θ] × [sin θ cos2 θ / (1 − sin θ)] = 2 sin θ / cos θ

⇒ 2 tan θ

∴ The correct answer is 2 tan θ.

Additional Information

Pythagorean Identities

Standard identities like sin2 θ + cos2 θ = 1, sec2 θ − tan2 θ = 1, and csc2 θ − cot2 θ = 1 are essential for simplifying trig expressions.

Sum and Difference Formula

The expansion of (a + b + c)2 = a2 + b2 + c2 + 2ab + 2bc + 2ca is frequently used to simplify squared trigonometric binomials or trinomials.

Reciprocal Relations

The sum tan θ + cot θ can always be rewritten as 1 / (sin θ cos θ) or sec θ csc θ.

questions.question: The value of \(\rm \frac{(cos\,9^\circ+sin \,81^\circ)(sec\,9^\circ+cosec\,81^\circ)}{cosec^2\,71^\circ+cos^2\,15^\circ-tan^2\,19^\circ+cos^2\,75^\circ} \) is:
questions.questionHtml: The value of \(\rm \frac{(cos\,9^\circ+sin \,81^\circ)(sec\,9^\circ+cosec\,81^\circ)}{cosec^2\,71^\circ+cos^2\,15^\circ-tan^2\,19^\circ+cos^2\,75^\circ} \) is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Use complementary angles: sin 81° = cos 9° and cosec 81° = sec 9°.

Numerator becomes (2 cos 9°) × (2 sec 9°) = 4 × (cos 9° × sec 9°) = 4.

In denominator, cosec² 71° = sec² 19° and cos² 75° = sin² 15°.

Denominator becomes (sec² 19° − tan² 19°) + (cos² 15° + sin² 15°) = 1 + 1 = 2.

Result = 4 ÷ 2 = 2.

∴ The correct answer is 2.

Alternate Method

Given: [(cos 9° + sin 81°)(sec 9° + cosec 81°)] ÷ [cosec² 71° + cos² 15° − tan² 19° + cos² 75°]

Formula Used: sin(90°−θ) = cosθ, cosec(90°−θ) = secθ, cos(90°−θ) = sinθ, sec²θ − tan²θ = 1, sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, cosθ × secθ = 1

⇒ Numerator = (cos 9° + sin(90°−9°)) × (sec 9° + cosec(90°−9°))

⇒ Numerator = (cos 9° + cos 9°) × (sec 9° + sec 9°)

⇒ Numerator = (2 cos 9°) × (2 sec 9°) = 4 × (cos 9° × sec 9°) = 4 × 1 = 4

⇒ Denominator = cosec²(90°−19°) − tan² 19° + cos² 15° + cos²(90°−15°)

⇒ Denominator = (sec² 19° − tan² 19°) + (cos² 15° + sin² 15°)

⇒ Denominator = 1 + 1 = 2

⇒ Value of expression = 4 ÷ 2 = 2

∴ The correct answer is 2.

Additional Information

Complementary Angle Identities

For any angle θ, sin(90°−θ) = cosθ, tan(90°−θ) = cotθ, and sec(90°−θ) = cosecθ.

Fundamental Trigonometric Identities

Standard identities include sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, sec²θ − tan²θ = 1, and cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1.

Reciprocal Relations

Trigonometric ratios are related as sinθ × cosecθ = 1, cosθ × secθ = 1, and tanθ × cotθ = 1.

questions.question: In ΔABC, ∠A = 50°, BE and CF are perpendiculars on AC and AB at E and F, respectively. BE and CF intersect at H. The bisectors of ∠HBC and ∠HCB intersect at P. ∠BPC is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: In ΔABC, ∠A = 50°, BE and CF are perpendiculars on AC and AB at E and F, respectively. BE and CF intersect at H. The bisectors of ∠HBC and ∠HCB intersect at P. ∠BPC is equal to:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Angle at Orthocenter (H): ∠BHC = 180° − ∠A

Angle at Incenter (P) of ΔHBC: ∠BPC = 90° + ∠BHC / 2

Combining the two: ∠BPC = 90° + (180° − ∠A) / 2 = 180° − ∠A / 2

Substituting ∠A = 50°: ∠BPC = 180° − 50° / 2 = 180° − 25° = 155°.

∴ The correct answer is 155°.

Alternate Method

Given: ∠A = 50° in ΔABC. BE and CF are altitudes intersecting at H. P is the intersection of bisectors of ∠HBC and ∠HCB.

Formula Used:

1. Angle formed by altitudes at orthocenter: ∠BHC = 180° − ∠A

2. Angle formed by interior angle bisectors in ΔHBC: ∠BPC = 90° + ∠BHC / 2

Calculations:

⇒ In quadrilateral AFHE, ∠AFH = 90° and ∠AEH = 90°.

⇒ Sum of angles in AFHE = 360°

⇒ ∠A + ∠AFH + ∠AEH + ∠FHE = 360°

⇒ 50° + 90° + 90° + ∠FHE = 360°

⇒ ∠FHE = 360° − 230° = 130°

⇒ ∠BHC = ∠FHE = 130° (Vertically opposite angles)

⇒ In ΔHBC, P is the incenter because it is the intersection of angle bisectors.

⇒ ∠BPC = 90° + ∠BHC / 2

⇒ ∠BPC = 90° + 130° / 2

⇒ ∠BPC = 90° + 65° = 155°.

∴ The correct answer is 155°.

Additional Information

Orthocenter Property

The angle subtended by any side at the orthocenter (H) is supplementary to the opposite vertex angle: ∠BHC + ∠A = 180°.

Incenter Angle Formula

The angle formed by interior angle bisectors at the incenter (I) is ∠BIC = 90° + ∠A / 2.

Circumcenter Angle Formula

The angle subtended by a side at the circumcenter (O) is twice the angle at the vertex: ∠BOC = 2 × ∠A.

Ex-center Angle Formula

The angle formed by the intersection of exterior angle bisectors at the ex-center (E) is ∠BEC = 90° − ∠A / 2.

questions.question: If \(\rm \frac{sin^2\,θ}{cos^2\,θ-3cos\,θ+2} \) = 1, θ lies in the first quadrant, then the value of \(\rm \frac{tan^2\frac{\theta}{2} +sin^2\frac{\theta}{2} }{tan\,\theta+sin\,\theta} \) is:
questions.questionHtml: If \(\rm \frac{sin^2\,θ}{cos^2\,θ-3cos\,θ+2} \) = 1, θ lies in the first quadrant, then the value of \(\rm \frac{tan^2\frac{\theta}{2} +sin^2\frac{\theta}{2} }{tan\,\theta+sin\,\theta} \) is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

From sin2θ / (cos2θ − 3cosθ + 2) = 1, equate numerator and denominator: 1 − cos2θ = cos2θ − 3cosθ + 2.

Simplifying, 2cos2θ − 3cosθ + 1 = 0 ⇒ (2cosθ − 1)(cosθ − 1) = 0.

In first quadrant, θ ≠ 0, so cosθ = 1/2 ⇒ θ = 60°.

Substitute θ = 60° and θ/2 = 30°: (tan230° + sin230°) / (tan60° + sin60°).

(1/3 + 1/4) / (√3 + √3/2) = (7/12) / (3√3/2) = 14 / (36√3) = 7 / (18√3) = 7√3/54.

∴ The correct answer is 7√3/54.

Alternate Method

Given: sin2θ / (cos2θ − 3cosθ + 2) = 1 and θ is in the first quadrant.

Formula Used: sin2θ = 1 − cos2θ; tan 30° = 1/√3; sin 30° = 1/2; tan 60° = √3; sin 60° = √3/2.

⇒ sin2θ = cos2θ − 3cosθ + 2

⇒ 1 − cos2θ = cos2θ − 3cosθ + 2

⇒ 2cos2θ − 3cosθ + 1 = 0

⇒ (2cosθ − 1)(cosθ − 1) = 0

⇒ cosθ = 1/2 or cosθ = 1

⇒ Since 0° < θ < 90°, cosθ = 1/2 ∴ θ = 60° and θ/2 = 30°.

⇒ Numerator = tan230° + sin230° = (1/√3)2 + (1/2)2 = 1/3 + 1/4 = 7/12

⇒ Denominator = tan60° + sin60° = √3 + √3/2 = 3√3/2

⇒ Expression = (7/12) ÷ (3√3/2) = (7/12) × (2 / 3√3) = 14 / 36√3 = 7 / 18√3

⇒ Rationalizing: (7 × √3) / (18√3 × √3) = 7√3 / 54.

∴ The correct answer is 7√3/54.

Additional Information

Pythagorean Identities

Fundamental relation between sine and cosine: sin2θ + cos2θ = 1. Useful for converting squared terms.

Quadratic Equations in Trigonometry

Equations like acos2θ + bcosθ + c = 0 are solved by treating cosθ as a variable, ensuring the root lies between −1 and 1.

Half-Angle Values

Special values for 30°: sin 30° = 1/2, cos 30° = √3/2, tan 30° = 1/√3. For 60°: sin 60° = √3/2, cos 60° = 1/2, tan 60° = √3.

questions.question: Three sides of a triangle are \(\sqrt{a^2+b^2} , \sqrt{(2a)^2+b^2} \) and \(\sqrt{a^2+(2b)^2} \) units. What is the area (in unit squares) of the triangle?
questions.questionHtml: Three sides of a triangle are \(\sqrt{a^2+b^2} , \sqrt{(2a)^2+b^2} \) and \(\sqrt{a^2+(2b)^2} \) units. What is the area (in unit squares) of the triangle?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The sides represent a triangle with vertices at (0, 0), (a, 2b), and (2a, b) in a coordinate plane.

Using the area formula for a triangle with one vertex at the origin: Area = 1/2 |x1y2 − x2y1|

Here, (x1, y1) = (a, 2b) and (x2, y2) = (2a, b).

Area = 1/2 |a × b − 2a × 2b| = 1/2 |ab − 4ab| = 1/2 |−3ab| = 1.5ab.

∴ The correct answer is 3/2 ab unit squares.

Alternate Method

Given:

Side 1 = √(a2 + b2)

Side 2 = √((2a)2 + b2) = √(4a2 + b2)

Side 3 = √(a2 + (2b)2) = √(a2 + 4b2)

Imagine the triangle enclosed within a rectangle of dimensions 2a × 2b with vertices at (0,0), (2a,0), (2a,2b), and (0,2b).

The area of the triangle can be calculated by subtracting the areas of three right-angled triangles from the total area of the 2a × 2b rectangle.

⇒ Total Area of Rectangle = 2a × 2b = 4ab

⇒ Area of Triangle 1 (base 2a, height b) = 1/2 × 2a × b = ab

⇒ Area of Triangle 2 (base a, height 2b) = 1/2 × a × 2b = ab

⇒ Area of Triangle 3 (base a, height b) = 1/2 × (2a − a) × (2b − b) = 1/2 × a × b = 0.5ab

⇒ Required Area = Total Area − (Area 1 + Area 2 + Area 3)

⇒ Required Area = 4ab − (ab + ab + 0.5ab)

⇒ Required Area = 4ab − 2.5ab = 1.5ab

⇒ Required Area = 3/2 ab

∴ The correct answer is 3/2 ab unit squares.

Additional Information

Coordinate Area Formula

For vertices (x1, y1), (x2, y2), and (x3, y3), Area = 1/2 |x1(y2−y3) + x2(y3−y1) + x3(y1−y2)|.

Distance Formula

The distance between two points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) is given by d = √((x2−x1)2 + (y2−y1)2).

Shoelace Theorem

A general algorithm to find the area of any polygon by summing the cross-products of the coordinates of its vertices.

questions.question: In an examination, the number of students who passed and the number of students who failed were in the ratio 25 ∶ 4. If one more student had appeared and passed and the number of failed students was 3 less than earlier, the ratio of passed students to failed students would have become 22 ∶ 3. What is the difference between the number of students who, initially, passed the examination and the number of students who failed the examination?
questions.questionHtml: In an examination, the number of students who passed and the number of students who failed were in the ratio 25 ∶ 4. If one more student had appeared and passed and the number of failed students was 3 less than earlier, the ratio of passed students to failed students would have become 22 ∶ 3. What is the difference between the number of students who, initially, passed the examination and the number of students who failed the examination?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Initial ratio of Passed students to Failed students is 25 : 4.

The difference between Passed and Failed students = 25 − 4 = 21 units.

The required answer must be a multiple of 21.

Checking the given options: 132, 126, 174, and 150.

Only 126 is exactly divisible by 21 (21 × 6 = 126).

∴ The correct answer is 126.

Alternate Method

Given: Initial ratio of Passed : Failed = 25 : 4.

Formula Used: Total Students = Passed + Failed

⇒ Let initial Passed = 25x and initial Failed = 4x.

⇒ Initial Total Students = 25x + 4x = 29x.

⇒ According to the condition, 1 more student appears and passes: New Total = 29x + 1.

⇒ New Failed students = 4x − 3.

⇒ New Passed students = Total − Failed = (29x + 1) − (4x − 3) = 25x + 4.

⇒ New Ratio (Passed : Failed) = 22 : 3.

⇒ (25x + 4) / (4x − 3) = 22 / 3

⇒ 3 × (25x + 4) = 22 × (4x − 3)

⇒ 75x + 12 = 88x − 66

⇒ 13x = 78 ⇒ x = 6.

⇒ Initial Passed = 25 × 6 = 150.

⇒ Initial Failed = 4 × 6 = 24.

⇒ Difference = 150 − 24 = 126.

∴ The correct answer is 126.

Additional Information

Compound Ratio

When two or more ratios are multiplied together (a/b × c/d), the result (ac/bd) is called the compound ratio.

Ratio and Proportionality

If a : b = c : d, then the product of extremes equals the product of means (ad = bc).

Cross-Product Method

A shortcut for ratio change problems where (Initial Ratio Part × Final Ratio Part − Initial Ratio Part × Final Ratio Part) accounts for absolute changes.

questions.question: In ΔPQR, the bisector of ∠R meets side PQ at S, PR = 10 cm, RQ = 14 cm and PQ = 12 cm. What is the length of SQ ?
questions.questionHtml: In ΔPQR, the bisector of ∠R meets side PQ at S, PR = 10 cm, RQ = 14 cm and PQ = 12 cm. What is the length of SQ ?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Angle Bisector Theorem states that the ratio of segments PS : SQ is equal to the ratio of sides PR : RQ.

Side ratio PR : RQ = 10 : 14 = 5 : 7.

Total ratio parts for PQ = 5 + 7 = 12 parts.

Given PQ = 12 cm, so 12 parts = 12 cm → 1 part = 1 cm.

Length of SQ = 7 parts = 7 × 1 = 7 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 7 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

In ΔPQR, PR = 10 cm, RQ = 14 cm, PQ = 12 cm.

RS is the internal bisector of ∠R meeting PQ at S.

Formula Used:

Internal Angle Bisector Theorem: PR / RQ = PS / SQ

Calculations:

⇒ PR / RQ = PS / SQ

⇒ 10 / 14 = PS / SQ

⇒ 5 / 7 = PS / SQ

⇒ Let PS = 5x and SQ = 7x

⇒ PS + SQ = PQ

⇒ 5x + 7x = 12

⇒ 12x = 12

⇒ x = 1

⇒ SQ = 7x = 7 × 1

⇒ SQ = 7 cm

∴ The correct answer is 7 cm.

Additional Information

Internal Angle Bisector Theorem

The bisector of an interior angle of a triangle divides the opposite side into segments whose lengths have the same ratio as the other two sides of the triangle.

External Angle Bisector Theorem

The bisector of an exterior angle of a triangle divides the opposite side externally in the ratio of the sides containing the angle.

Length of the Bisector

The length of the internal bisector RS can be calculated using the formula: RS2 = (PR × RQ) − (PS × SQ).

questions.question: If \(x+\frac{1}{x} = 3\) , x ≠ 0, then the value of \(x^7+\frac{1}{x^7} \) is:
questions.questionHtml: If \(x+\frac{1}{x} = 3\), x ≠ 0, then the value of \(x^7+\frac{1}{x^7} \) is:

So, x7 + 1/x7 = 18 × 47 - 3 ⇒ 846 - 3 ⇒ 843

questions.question: In equilateral ΔABC, D and E are points on the sides AB and AC, respectively, such that AD = CE. BE and CD intersect at F. The measure (in degrees) of ∠CFB is:
questions.questionHtml: In equilateral ΔABC, D and E are points on the sides AB and AC, respectively, such that AD = CE. BE and CD intersect at F. The measure (in degrees) of ∠CFB is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In equilateral ΔABC, AD = CE implies that ΔADC ≅ ΔCEB by the SAS property.

By CPCT, the corresponding angles ∠ACD and ∠CBE are equal.

In ΔBFC, the sum of base angles is ∠BCF + ∠CBF = (60° − ∠ACD) + ∠CBE = 60°.

The internal angle ∠CFB = 180° − (Sum of base angles) = 180° − 60° = 120°.

∴ The correct answer is 120°.

Alternate Method

Given: ΔABC is an equilateral triangle. D is on AB and E is on AC such that AD = CE.

Formula Used: SAS (Side-Angle-Side) Congruence and Angle Sum Property of a triangle.

⇒ In ΔADC and ΔCEB:

⇒ AC = BC (Sides of an equilateral triangle)

⇒ ∠DAC = ∠ECB = 60° (Angles of an equilateral triangle)

⇒ AD = CE (Given)

⇒ ∴ ΔADC ≅ ΔCEB (By SAS Congruence)

⇒ ∠ACD = ∠CBE (By CPCT)

⇒ In ΔBFC, ∠BCF = ∠BCA − ∠ACD = 60° − ∠ACD

⇒ ∠CBF = ∠CBE

⇒ ∠CFB = 180° − (∠BCF + ∠CBF)

⇒ ∠CFB = 180° − (60° − ∠ACD + ∠CBE)

⇒ Since ∠ACD = ∠CBE, ∠CFB = 180° − 60°

⇒ ∠CFB = 120°.

∴ The correct answer is 120°.

Additional Information

Equilateral Triangle Properties

All internal angles are equal to 60° and all sides are of equal length.

SAS Congruence Rule

Two triangles are congruent if two sides and the included angle of one triangle are equal to the corresponding sides and included angle of the other.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all internal angles in any triangle is always 180°.

Exterior Angle Property

The exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles.

questions.question: The volume of a right circular cone is 308 cm 3 and the radius of its base is 7 cm. What is the curved surface area (in cm 2 ) of the cone? (Take π = \(\frac{22}{7} \) )
questions.questionHtml: The volume of a right circular cone is 308 cm3 and the radius of its base is 7 cm. What is the curved surface area (in cm2) of the cone? (Take π = \(\frac{22}{7} \))
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Height (h) = (3 × Volume) ÷ (π × r2)

h = (3 × 308) ÷ (22/7 × 7 × 7) = (3 × 308) ÷ 154 = 6 cm.

Slant height (l) = √(r2 + h2) = √(72 + 62) = √85 cm.

Curved Surface Area = πrl = (22/7) × 7 × √85 = 22√85 cm2.

∴ The correct answer is 22√85 cm2.

Alternate Method

Given:

Volume (V) = 308 cm3

Radius (r) = 7 cm

Formula Used:

Volume of cone = (1/3) × π × r2 × h

Slant height (l) = √(r2 + h2)

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = π × r × l

Calculations:

⇒ 308 = (1/3) × (22/7) × 7 × 7 × h

⇒ 308 = (1/3) × 22 × 7 × h

⇒ 308 = (154/3) × h

⇒ h = (308 × 3) ÷ 154

⇒ h = 2 × 3 = 6 cm

⇒ l = √(72 + 62)

⇒ l = √(49 + 36) = √85 cm

⇒ CSA = (22/7) × 7 × √85

⇒ CSA = 22√85 cm2

∴ The correct answer is 22√85 cm2.

Additional Information

Total Surface Area of Cone

The total surface area (TSA) includes the CSA plus the area of the circular base: TSA = πrl + πr2 = πr(l + r).

Slant Height Property

In a right circular cone, the height (h), radius (r), and slant height (l) always form a right-angled triangle, satisfying l2 = r2 + h2.

Volume Relation

The volume of a cone is exactly one-third the volume of a cylinder having the same base radius and height.

questions.question: In ΔABC, D is a point on BC such that ∠ADB = 2∠DAC, ∠BAC = 70° and ∠B = 56°. What is the measure of ∠ADC?
questions.questionHtml: In ΔABC, D is a point on BC such that ∠ADB = 2∠DAC, ∠BAC = 70° and ∠B = 56°. What is the measure of ∠ADC?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

First, find ∠C = 180° − (70° + 56°) = 54°.

In ΔADC, ∠ADB is the exterior angle: ∠ADB = ∠DAC + ∠C.

Substitute given ∠ADB = 2∠DAC ⇒ 2∠DAC = ∠DAC + 54°.

∴ ∠DAC = 54°.

Measure of ∠ADC = 180° − ∠ADB = 180° − 2(54°) = 72°.

∴ The correct answer is 72°.

Alternate Method

Given: ∠BAC = 70°, ∠B = 56°, ∠ADB = 2∠DAC.

Formula: Angle sum property of Δ is 180°; Exterior angle = Sum of two opposite interior angles.

In ΔABC:

⇒ ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°

⇒ 70° + 56° + ∠C = 180°

⇒ 126° + ∠C = 180°

⇒ ∠C = 54°

Now, let ∠DAC = x.

⇒ ∠ADB = 2x (Given)

In ΔADC, ∠ADB is an exterior angle to ∠DAC and ∠C:

⇒ ∠ADB = ∠DAC + ∠C

⇒ 2x = x + 54°

⇒ x = 54°

We need to find ∠ADC:

⇒ ∠ADC = 180° − ∠ADB (Linear Pair)

⇒ ∠ADC = 180° − 2x

⇒ ∠ADC = 180° − 2(54°)

⇒ ∠ADC = 180° − 108°

⇒ ∠ADC = 72°

∴ The correct answer is 72°.

Additional Information

Exterior Angle Theorem

The exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles. In ΔADC, ∠ADB = ∠DAC + ∠ACD.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all interior angles of any triangle is always 180°.

Linear Pair Axiom

If a ray stands on a line, then the sum of two adjacent angles so formed is 180°. Here, ∠ADB + ∠ADC = 180°.

questions.question: The ratio of the investments of A and B in a business is 7 ∶ 5, and the ratio of their profits at the end of a year is 2 ∶ 5. If A invested the money for 6 months, then for how much time (in months) has B invested his money?
questions.questionHtml: The ratio of the investments of A and B in a business is 7 ∶ 5, and the ratio of their profits at the end of a year is 2 ∶ 5. If A invested the money for 6 months, then for how much time (in months) has B invested his money?
questions.solution:
The ratio of investments of A and B = 7 : 5 and the ratio of profits of A and B = 2 : 5

We know that, Time = Profit/Investment

The ratio of time = \(\frac{2}{7}: \frac{5}{5}\)

Investment time of A and B = 2 : 7

Now investments time of A = 2 ——→ 6 months

So investment time of B = 7  ——→ 21 months

questions.question: A cylindrical tube, open at both ends, is made of a metal sheet which is 0.5 cm thick. Its outer radius is 4 cm and length is 2 m. How much metal (in cm 3 ) has been used in making the tube?
questions.questionHtml: A cylindrical tube, open at both ends, is made of a metal sheet which is 0.5 cm thick. Its outer radius is 4 cm and length is 2 m. How much metal (in cm<sup>3</sup>) has been used in making the tube?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Volume of metal in a hollow cylinder = π × (R + r)(R − r) × h

Outer radius R = 4 cm, Inner radius r = 4 − 0.5 = 3.5 cm

Length h = 2 m = 200 cm

Volume = π × (4 + 3.5) × (4 − 3.5) × 200 = π × 7.5 × 0.5 × 200

Volume = π × 3.75 × 200 = 750π cm3

∴ The correct answer is 750π cm3.

Alternate Method

Given:

Outer radius (R) = 4 cm

Thickness of sheet = 0.5 cm

Length of tube (h) = 2 m = 200 cm

Formula Used:

Volume of metal = Volume of Outer Cylinder − Volume of Inner Cylinder = πR2h − πr2h

Calculations:

⇒ Inner radius (r) = Outer radius − Thickness

⇒ r = 4 − 0.5 = 3.5 cm

⇒ Volume of metal = π × (R2 − r2) × h

⇒ Volume = π × (42 − 3.52) × 200

⇒ Volume = π × (16 − 12.25) × 200

⇒ Volume = π × 3.75 × 200

⇒ Volume = 750π cm3

∴ The correct answer is 750π cm3.

Additional Information

Surface Area of Hollow Cylinder

Total Surface Area = 2π(R + r)(h + R − r), where R is outer radius and r is inner radius.

Curved Surface Area

CSA of hollow cylinder = 2πRh + 2πrh = 2πh(R + r).

Conversion Unit

Always ensure all units are consistent: 1 meter = 100 centimeters.

questions.question: If x 4 + y 4 + x 2 y 2 = \(17\frac{1}{16}\) and x 2 – xy + y 2 = \(5\frac{1}{4}\) , then one of the values of (x – y) is:
questions.questionHtml: If x4 + y4 + x2y2 = \(17\frac{1}{16}\) and x2 – xy + y2 = \(5\frac{1}{4}\), then one of the values of (x – y) is:
questions.solution:
⇒ a4 + b4 + a2b2 = (a2 – ab + b2) (a2 + ab + b2)

⇒ x4 + y4 + x2y2 = (x2 – xy + y2) (x2 + xy + y2) ⇒ \(17\frac{1}{16}\) = \(5\frac{1}{4}\) (x2 + xy + y2)

⇒ (x2 + xy + y2) = \(\frac{13}{4}\) → (i)

On adding  x2 – xy + y2 = \(5\frac{1}{4}\) and (i), we get  (x2 + y2) = \(\frac{17}{4}\) → (ii)

Subtract x2 – xy + y2 = \(5\frac{1}{4}\)  form (i), we get xy = -1 → (iii)

Now, Using the formula (a - b)2 = a2 + b2 - 2ab, (x - y)2 = x2 + y2 - 2xy

From (ii) and (iii), we get (x - y)2 = (17/4) - 2 × (-1) ⇒ (x - y)2 = (17/4) + 2 = 25/4

⇒ (x - y) = 5/2.

questions.question: The base of a right pyramid is a square of side \(8\sqrt{2} \) cm and each of its slant edge is of length 10 cm. What is the volume (in cm 3 ) of the pyramid?
questions.questionHtml: The base of a right pyramid is a square of side \(8\sqrt{2} \) cm and each of its slant edge is of length 10 cm. What is the volume (in cm3) of the pyramid?
questions.solution:

Right angle-triangle OPD, OP2 = OD2 - DP2 ⇒ OP2 = 102 - 82 = 62 ⇒ OP = 6

questions.question: The base of a right prism is a triangle whose sides are 8 cm, 15 cm and 17 cm, and its lateral surface area is 480 cm 2 . What is the volume (in cm 3 ) of the prism?
questions.questionHtml: The base of a right prism is a triangle whose sides are 8 cm, 15 cm and 17 cm, and its lateral surface area is 480 cm<sup>2</sup>. What is the volume (in cm<sup>3</sup>) of the prism?
questions.solution:

Volume of prism = area × height = 60 × 12 = 720 cm3.

questions.question: X and Y travel a distance of 90 km each such that the speed of Y is greater than that of X. The sum of their speeds is 100 km/h and the total time taken by both is 3 hours 45 minutes. The ratio of the speed of X to that of Y is:
questions.questionHtml: X and Y travel a distance of 90 km each such that the speed of Y is greater than that of X. The sum of their speeds is 100 km/h and the total time taken by both is 3 hours 45 minutes. The ratio of the speed of X to that of Y is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total time = 3 hours 45 minutes = 3.75 hours.

Product of speeds (Sx × Sy) = (Distance × Sum of speeds) ÷ Total time.

Product = (90 × 100) ÷ 3.75 = 2400.

Identify two numbers whose sum is 100 and product is 2400 → 40 and 60.

Since Speed Y > Speed X, Speed X = 40 km/h and Speed Y = 60 km/h.

Ratio of X : Y = 40 : 60 = 2 : 3.

∴ The correct answer is 2 : 3.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total Distance = 90 km each

Sum of speeds (Sx + Sy) = 100 km/h

Total time = 3 hours + 45/60 hours = 3.75 hours

Formula Used:

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Calculations:

⇒ Total Time = (90/Sx) + (90/Sy) = 3.75

⇒ 90 × [(Sx + Sy) / (Sx × Sy)] = 3.75

⇒ 90 × [100 / (Sx × Sy)] = 3.75

⇒ 9000 / (Sx × Sy) = 3.75

⇒ Sx × Sy = 9000 / 3.75 = 2400

⇒ Let speeds be roots of k2 − (Sum)k + Product = 0

⇒ k2 − 100k + 2400 = 0

⇒ k2 − 60k − 40k + 2400 = 0

⇒ (k − 60)(k − 40) = 0

⇒ k = 60 or 40

⇒ Since Sy > Sx, Sy = 60 km/h and Sx = 40 km/h

⇒ Ratio Sx : Sy = 40 : 60 = 2 : 3

∴ The correct answer is 2 : 3.

Additional Information

Average Speed

When a person travels the same distance at two different speeds x and y, the average speed is given by (2xy)/(x + y).

Inverse Proportion of Speed and Time

For a constant distance, speed is inversely proportional to time. If speed ratio is a:b, time ratio will be b:a.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

questions.question: If a nine-digit number 789x6378y is divisible by 72, then the value of xy is:
questions.questionHtml: If a nine-digit number 789x6378y is divisible by 72, then the value of xy is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Divisibility by 72 means the number must be divisible by both 8 and 9.

For divisibility by 8, last 3 digits 78y must be divisible by 8 ⇒ 784 ÷ 8 = 98, so y = 4.

For divisibility by 9, Sum of digits (7+8+9+x+6+3+7+8+4) = 52 + x must be divisible by 9.

Nearest multiple of 9 after 52 is 54 ⇒ 52 + x = 54 ⇒ x = 2.

Value of xy = 2 × 4 = 8.

∴ The correct answer is 8.

Alternate Method

Given: Nine-digit number 789x6378y is divisible by 72.

Formula Used: Divisibility rules for 8 (last 3 digits) and 9 (sum of digits).

⇒ Number = 789x6378y

⇒ Divisibility by 8: Check 78y. Dividing 780 by 8 gives remainder 4. Next multiple is 784.

⇒ y = 4

⇒ Divisibility by 9: Sum = 7 + 8 + 9 + x + 6 + 3 + 7 + 8 + 4

⇒ Sum = 52 + x

⇒ For 52 + x to be divisible by 9, x must be 2 (as 54 is the nearest multiple).

⇒ x = 2

⇒ Value of xy = x × y = 2 × 4 = 8

∴ The correct answer is 8.

Additional Information

Divisibility by 8

A number is divisible by 8 if its last three digits are divisible by 8 or if they are 000.

Divisibility by 9

A number is divisible by 9 if the sum of all its digits is divisible by 9.

Divisibility by Composite Numbers

To check divisibility by a composite number (like 72), check for its coprime factors (8 and 9 in this case).

questions.question: The curved surface area of a right circular cone is 2310 cm 2 and its radius is 21 cm. If its radius is increased by 100% and height is reduced by 50%, then its capacity (in litres) will be (correct to one decimal place): (Take π = \(\frac{22}{7}\) )
questions.questionHtml:
The curved surface area of a right circular cone is 2310 cm2 and its radius is 21 cm. If its radius is increased by 100% and height is reduced by 50%, then its capacity (in litres) will be (correct to one decimal place):

(Take π = \(\frac{22}{7}\))
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Slant height l = CSA ÷ (πr) = 2310 ÷ (22/7 × 21) = 35 cm.

Height h = √(l2 − r2) = √(352 − 212) = 28 cm.

New r = 2r = 42 cm and New h = h/2 = 14 cm.

New Volume = 2 × Initial Volume = 2 × (1/3 × 22/7 × 212 × 28) = 25872 cm3.

Capacity = 25872 ÷ 1000 = 25.872 litres ≈ 25.9 litres.

∴ The correct answer is 25.9 litres.

Alternate Method

Given: Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2310 cm2, Radius (r) = 21 cm.

Formula used: CSA = πrl, h2 = l2 − r2, Volume (V) = (1/3)πr2h.

⇒ 2310 = (22/7) × 21 × l

⇒ 2310 = 66 × l ⇒ l = 2310 ÷ 66 = 35 cm

⇒ h = √(352 − 212) = √(1225 − 441) = √784 = 28 cm

⇒ New radius (r') = 21 + 100% of 21 = 42 cm

⇒ New height (h') = 28 − 50% of 28 = 14 cm

⇒ New Volume (V') = 1/3 × 22/7 × 42 × 42 × 14

⇒ V' = 22 × 2 × 42 × 14 = 25872 cm3

⇒ Capacity in litres = 25872 ÷ 1000 = 25.872 litres

⇒ Rounded to one decimal place = 25.9 litres

∴ The correct answer is 25.9 litres.

Additional Information

Total Surface Area (TSA) of a Cone

The total surface area includes the curved surface and the base area: TSA = πrl + πr2 = πr(l + r).

Unit Conversion (Volume)

1 litre = 1000 cm3 | 1 m3 = 1000 litres.

Slant Height Calculation

For any right circular cone, slant height (l), radius (r), and height (h) form a right-angled triangle: l2 = r2 + h2.

Effect of Dimension Changes on Volume

If radius is scaled by x and height by y, then the volume is scaled by x2 × y.

questions.question: Study the given histogram and answer the question that follows. The total number of neon lamps having lifetime of 800 or more hours is approximately what percentage more than the total number of neon lamps having lifetime of 400 or more hours but less than 800 hours?
questions.questionHtml:
Study the given histogram and answer the question that follows.

The total number of neon lamps having lifetime of 800 or more hours is approximately what percentage more than the total number of neon lamps having lifetime of 400 or more hours but less than 800 hours?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Lamps (800+ hours) = 80 + 145 = 225

Lamps (400−800 hours) = 14 + 56 + 60 + 70 = 200

Required percentage = [(225 − 200) ÷ 200] × 100

Required percentage = [25 ÷ 200] × 100 = 12.5%

∴ The correct answer is 12.5%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Lamps in lifetime 400-500 = 14

Lamps in lifetime 500-600 = 56

Lamps in lifetime 600-700 = 60

Lamps in lifetime 700-800 = 70

Lamps in lifetime 800-900 = 80

Lamps in lifetime 900-1000 = 145

Formula Used:

Percentage More = [(Value1 − Value2) ÷ Value2] × 100

Calculations:

⇒ Total lamps with lifetime 800 or more hours (Value1) = 80 + 145 = 225

⇒ Total lamps with lifetime 400 to 800 hours (Value2) = 14 + 56 + 60 + 70 = 200

⇒ Difference = 225 − 200 = 25

⇒ Percentage more = (25 ÷ 200) × 100

⇒ Percentage more = 0.125 × 100 = 12.5%

∴ The correct answer is 12.5%.

Additional Information

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage change = (Final Value − Initial Value) ÷ Initial Value × 100. Always divide by the 'than' or base value.

The area or height of each bar represents the frequency (number of lamps) for a specific continuous class interval (lifetime in hours).

questions.question: In ΔPQR, PQ = PR and S is a point on QR such that ∠PSQ = 96° + ∠QPS and ∠QPR = 132°. What is the measure of ∠PSR?
questions.questionHtml: In ΔPQR, PQ = PR and S is a point on QR such that ∠PSQ = 96° + ∠QPS and ∠QPR = 132°. What is the measure of ∠PSR?
questions.solution:
Let ∠QPS be θ

⇒ ∠PSQ = 96° + θ

Now, In ΔPQR, ∠Q + ∠R = 180° - ∠P

⇒ ∠Q + ∠R = 180° -132°  = 48° 

We know, ∠Q = ∠R = 24°      [∵ PQ = PR]

Now, In ΔPQS, (96° + θ) + θ + 24° = 180° 

⇒ θ = 30°

⇒ ∠PSQ = 96° + 30° = 126° 

∠PSR = 180° - 126° = 54°

questions.question: The average of 25 numbers is 64. The averages of the first 13 numbers and that of the last 13 numbers are 62.8 and 72.2, respectively. If the 12 th number is 61, and if the 12 th and 13 th numbers are excluded, then what is the average of the remaining numbers (correct to one decimal place)?
questions.questionHtml: The average of 25 numbers is 64. The averages of the first 13 numbers and that of the last 13 numbers are 62.8 and 72.2, respectively. If the 12<sup>th</sup> number is 61, and if the 12<sup>th</sup> and 13<sup>th</sup> numbers are excluded, then what is the average of the remaining numbers (correct to one decimal place)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Net deviation of 26 numbers (first 13 + last 13) from the original average 64:

Deviation = 13 × (62.8 − 64) + 13 × (72.2 − 64) = 13 × (−1.2 + 8.2) = 13 × 7 = 91.

Since the 13th number is counted twice, 13th number = 64 + 91 = 155.

Sum of 12th and 13th numbers = 61 + 155 = 216.

New Average = (Total Sum − 216) ÷ (25 − 2) = (1600 − 216) ÷ 23 = 1384 ÷ 23 ≈ 60.2.

∴ The correct answer is 60.2.

Alternate Method

Given: Average of 25 numbers = 64 | Avg of first 13 = 62.8 | Avg of last 13 = 72.2 | 12th number = 61.

Formula: Sum = Average × Count

⇒ Total sum of 25 numbers = 25 × 64 = 1600

⇒ Sum of first 13 numbers = 13 × 62.8 = 816.4

⇒ Sum of last 13 numbers = 13 × 72.2 = 938.6

⇒ Sum of (1 to 13) + (13 to 25) = 816.4 + 938.6 = 1755

⇒ 13th number = 1755 − 1600 = 155

⇒ Sum of excluded numbers (12th + 13th) = 61 + 155 = 216

⇒ Sum of remaining 23 numbers = 1600 − 216 = 1384

⇒ Average of remaining numbers = 1384 ÷ 23 ≈ 60.173

∴ The correct answer is 60.2.

Additional Information

Deviation Method for Overlap

When one middle number is common in two groups, its value = Original Average + Total Deviation from the groups.

Exclusion Average Formula

New Average = (Initial Sum − Sum of Excluded Items) ÷ (Initial Count − Number of Excluded Items).

Weighted Average

The combined average of two groups is given by (n1×A1 + n2×A2) ÷ (n1 + n2).
